subject: history
title: Causes of War: Interpretations
welcome_lead: Today you'll judge historians' arguments — who was really to blame for war?
meta_desc: GCSE History Causes of War interpretations — blame, evidence and historians' debates.
final_note: You can now weigh different interpretations and use evidence to support a judgement.

concepts.def: A historian's argued view of the past
Argument that Germany planned WWI deliberately
Historian who challenges the standard view
Asking 'what if' a different choice had been made
Origin and purpose of a source

walkthroughs.body_html:
For decades blame shifted around Europe.

In 1961 the German historian Fritz Fischer argued Germany had aggressive plans before 1914. Others say all the great powers share blame — Austria-Hungary for the ultimatum, Russia for early mobilisation, Britain for ambiguity.

Critics say appeasement let Hitler grow stronger.

Defenders point out Britain was unready in 1938 and the public hated the idea of another war so soon after WWI. The 1938 Munich crowds cheered Neville Chamberlain — context matters.

To weigh an interpretation, check the source's provenance — who wrote it, when, and why.

A 1919 British speech blaming Germany has a clear purpose. A 1960s academic study uses archives unavailable in 1919. Both are useful — for different reasons.
